matrix.agreed_answer: Under regular profile-likelihood conditions, the likelihood-ratio statistic for a derived target g converges to chi-square with r degrees of freedom, where r is the local rank of g on identifiable fit directions.
matrix.adjudicated_correct: The Wilks tangent-space projection and the Gaussian Mahalanobis projection are mathematically equivalent in their common local-quadratic regime. The Gaussian expression rank(Dg C^(1/2)) is the identifiable-direction form of the Wilks codimension.

matrix.agreed_answer: At 68.27% confidence, a non-degenerate scalar target uses Delta chi-square = 1.00, while a joint target with two locally independent real components uses Delta chi-square = 2.2957489289, approximately 2.30.
matrix.adjudicated_correct: A separately quoted real or imaginary pole component is scalar and uses 1.00. A joint (Re E_pole, Im E_pole) contour uses 2.30 when the two directions are locally independent. Separate scalar intervals are not a 68.27% joint region.

matrix.agreed_answer: At each fixed abscissa a curve value is a scalar target and uses the one-dimensional threshold. A ribbon formed from those intervals has pointwise, not simultaneous, coverage; the number of plotted grid points is not the likelihood-ratio degrees of freedom.
matrix.adjudicated_correct: A simultaneous whole-curve statement requires calibration of a supremum statistic or projection of a joint confidence region for the identifiable curve directions. It cannot be obtained by setting ndof equal to the number of grid points.
